A record root has tagged false, because tagged needs a union root. So the mutant term never changes a result. A differential through checkRecursion tested 300000 random forged declarations and every report matched.

The mutant registers a group for a tagged component of one member that has no self edge. The reaches walk consults a group only when the source and the target are the same group. For a one-member group that means a self reference, which is a self edge of the graph, so the component is a cycle in the source too. A differential through checkRecursion tested 300000 random forged declarations, and every report matched. In a count over 100000 of them, 81276 held such a tagged singleton.

The mutant adds two cases. An acyclic tagged singleton gets a group that nothing consults, as the row for the length test explains. A cycle without a tagged member is made of aliases only, and the alias-only test keeps every edge of such a component, so the cycle test returns before a group is set. A differential through checkRecursion tested 300000 random forged declarations, and every report matched. In a count over 100000 of them, 1909 held an alias-only cycle of several members.

The mutant differs only when common equals the directory length of the source file. The second loop guard then holds, so to[common] is a string, while from[common] is undefined. The two never compare equal, so the loop stops under both guards. A differential over 339,000 path pairs of up to four segments matched.

The mutant differs only when the index of the hash equals the index of the colon. One index cannot hold both characters. When both are absent, the first term colon < 0 already returns undefined. A differential over all strings of up to six characters from `c a p : # . x` matched.
The mutant differs only when the dot is at index 0. A CapabilityId starts with `cap:`, so index 0 holds `c` (ir.ts:7). A differential over all `cap:` strings with up to six more characters matched.
The mutant differs only when `#` is at index 0. A CapabilityId starts with `cap:`, so index 0 holds `c` (ir.ts:7). A differential over all `cap:` strings with up to six more characters matched.

The dot search starts at the hash index, and the hash is not at index 0 for a CapabilityId. So a dot found is at an index of at least 1, and index 0 cannot hold it. A differential over all `cap:` strings with up to six more characters matched.

A stale change leaves the text and the version unchanged, so the mutant only marks the project dirty. A flush of a started project with no text difference starts no revision, and `#publish` sends a list only when its JSON or the version of its open document changed. A project that has not flushed is already dirty. A differential probe of six stale-change scenarios, at debounce 0 and 50 and with an `effektive/stats` request, matched.

With <=, a frame with no targets left runs one more pass. targets[frame.next] is undefined there, so index[undefined] < 0 and onStack[undefined] are both false, the pass changes nothing, and the next pass pops the frame as before.
With <=, the loop also reads index[count], which is undefined. undefined < 0 is false, so no node outside 0 .. count - 1 is visited and the result is the same.

With <=, the test also accepts index 0. Only node 0 gets index 0, because the loop visits it first at n = 0 while every index is -1. At every later n, index[n] is -1 or at least 1, so the visits are the same.

The walk never reaches depth 64. Only a member that is a named union alias deepens it: a union nested 70 levels inline emits Option.fromUndefinedOr(u.x). declaration/012 rejects a chain of 64 such aliases (U64 is nested deeper than 128 levels), and a chain of 63 emits the option read. So >= and > give the same result.
